rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=10, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=50, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.0003, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-8 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-7 hr=0.0, aggressive lr=3e-3 (n_iter=50) gave rmse=0.00657 (WORST of the run), ssim=0.931 -- the big step destabilized/over-smoothed. Best config remains iter-6: lr=3e-4, n_iter=50, rmse=0.00628. (2) FAILURE MODE: plain-UNet N2I regresses to the over-smoothed FBP mean; large lr worsens it. (3) ONE KNOB: relative to the BEST reference config (iter-6: warm_start=True, lr=3e-4, n_iter=50, pretrain_epochs=3), change ONLY pretrain_epochs 3 -> 10 (revert lr to iter-6's 3e-4). A stronger amortised warm-start = a better generic init for the 50-step per-image fits. (4) HYPOTHESIS: 10 warm-start epochs on the 400-scene train split give the denoisers a stronger, more detail-aware initialization, so the short 50-step per-image fit starts from a sharper point and lands at lower rmse. If hr rises, the warm-start init quality was the lever. Per the documented ceiling, more likely the amortised N2I warm-start ALSO converges to an over-smoothed mean (same GT-free FBP target), so a stronger warm-start just entrenches the blur (hr=0). (5) BUDGET: pretrain ep=10 (~430s) + 200*50-step fast fits (~400s) + figure ~= 15 min < 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-9 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: unet_c=8 (smaller), n_iter=100 mid, grad_clip off, seed variance check, pretrain_steps cap.
